title: Interchanging proper direct image and extension by zero
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $\Lambda$ be admissible in the sense of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use the finite-subextension condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], as fixed by the chapter. Let $p:\overline X\to Y$ be proper, let
$i:Y\to\overline Y$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, and let
$\overline X\xrightarrow{j'}W\xrightarrow{r}\overline Y$ be a compactification of
$i\circ p$ in the sense of [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], with $\overline X$ dense in $W$. Then:

1. $r^{-1}(Y)=\overline X$ (as open subschemes of $W$), and $r$ restricts to $p$
over $Y$;
2. for $A\in D(\overline X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ there is a unique map
$\iota_A:i_!Rp_*A\to Rr_*j'_!A$ in $D(\overline Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ whose
restriction to $Y$ is the identity of $Rp_*A$;
3. $\iota_A$ is an isomorphism for every $A\in\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: The source-library theorem Compactification.isPullback_of_isProper_of_isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant proves the compactification square cartesian: the restriction of the open immersion over Y is proper, hence closed, and scheme-theoretically dominant, hence an isomorphism. IsPullback.opensRange_fst on the flipped square gives the required equality of opens.

The proved cartesianDerivedCounit helper from the open base-change module makes the counit of j! ⊣ j* invertible on r* i! T. The open unit is invertible. Thus the left exchange mate of the canonical pullback comparison is invertible. An explicit unit/counit calculation identifies its conjugate under the composite adjunctions with the right exchange mate, namely compositionInterchangeRestriction. Hence the restriction comparison is invertible on every unbounded object.

Transpose Rp_* of the j-unit followed by the inverse restriction comparison through the i-open adjunction. The inverse identities give the normalization equation. Cancellation of the restriction comparison and injectivity of the adjunction hom equivalence give uniqueness.

Shrink finite coefficient carriers by a ring equivalence, with explicit continuous postcomposition isomorphisms of condensed rings. This converts the coefficient hypothesis to the finite-subextension admissibility convention. For a constructible finite-Tor generator A, j! A is constructible finite-Tor. Restrict it to the chosen pullback W ×_Ybar Y; open pullback preserves the generators. The cartesian-square isomorphism and the derived open counit identify extension by zero of that restriction with j! A itself. Apply proper_open_boundary_zero and transport along this isomorphism to obtain vanishing on the closed complement.

The boundary functor F = D(j!) ⋙ Rr_* ⋙ D(z*) is triangulated. Its zero kernel is replete and triangulated; intersecting it with Loc(Dctf) gives a localizing subcategory, because compactification_localizing supplies preservation of ambient sums and D(z*) is a left adjoint. Minimality of localizingClosure extends boundary vanishing from the generators to every A in Loc(Dctf). The source i! Rp_* A has zero closed restriction by disjoint support. Normalization and invertible open units show that the open restriction of the comparison is invertible. The proved source-library derived open–closed joint-reflection theorem now makes the comparison invertible.

proof_origin.place: Proof (1)–(3), realized by cartesian adjunction mates and a triangulated boundary-vanishing kernel. The unit composition route is unchanged.

The old steps 2-4 became lem-sfb-derived-open-square-restriction: open restriction commutes with Rr_* on unbounded categories for all admissible Λ, via a Hom chain made of D(i_!)⊣D(i*), r*⊣Rr_*, the open base change from open-closed (4), D(j_!)⊣D(j*) and p*⊣Rp_*. It is true, with no properness needed, and checked on small cases (r=id, i=id, W empty). The old step 6 became lem-sfb-proper-open-boundary-zero: c*Rr_*j_!A=0 for A in Dctf. It is true: j_!A is in Dctf by det-proper-image-localizing-open; proper base change uses the finite version (2) on Dctf, and the integral (3) and rational (3) versions on Dbc, since Dctf is contained in Dbc; and r^{-1}(Z) misses U. The item's statement and lean records are byte-identical to live, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Step 2's λ_A=(Rp_*η_{j'})^{-1}ρ type-checks. Step 3 is elementary adjunction calculus, with shift compatibility taken from node 1. Step 4 gets c*i_!=0 from open-closed (4). Step 5 uses exactness of the module pullbacks, open-closed detection (i is quasi-compact), coherence-single on (id,p), (i,id) and (j',r), and determination-localizing. Neither new node restates a parent clause, I found no cycle and no SGA citation, and the item is not in the dropped list.
